projects.name: MICROTECT
projects.summary: An automated optical detection system for identifying microplastics in rock salt using computer vision and an embedded Raspberry Pi workflow.
projects.impact: Positions the portfolio around real engineering systems that integrate AI, physical hardware, environmental monitoring, and operator-facing software.
projects.role: Capstone project lead, full-system developer, frontend UI/UX, backend processing logic, AI workflow, and hardware integration
highlights: Detected and quantified microplastic particles using YOLOv11 and optical imaging
Integrated Raspberry Pi 5, camera module, lighting control, and real-time UI
Developed the full operator workflow from image capture and detection to frontend UI, graph views, and reports

details.problem: Manual microscopy for microplastic inspection is slow, inconsistent, and difficult to repeat across multiple rock salt samples.
details.solution: Build a compact AI-assisted inspection system that captures sample images, detects particles, visualizes findings, and supports report generation.
details.architecture: Sample tray and optical capture setup -> Raspberry Pi 5 image processing -> backend detection and measurement logic -> YOLOv11 result handling -> touchscreen frontend UI -> report and graph outputs.
details.software: YOLOv11 detection pipeline with annotated training data, OpenCV image handling, backend processing logic, bounding-box identification, pixel-to-micrometer conversion, frontend result UI, UX flow, real-time feedback, graph views, and report generation.
results: Conducted multi-trial testing across different sample sources
Computed mean detection consistency of 69.71% based on microplastic count
Model performance: precision 0.826, recall 0.733, and mAP@50 of 0.814
Reduced dependence on fully manual visual inspection
challenges: Improved optical detection through controlled imaging and illumination
Handled varied particle appearance through dataset annotation and model evaluation
Designed the UI/UX around fast inspection, visualization, result reading, and documentation

projects.posterNote: AI detection | Raspberry Pi | environmental monitoring

projects.name: HerCare
projects.summary: A soft, supportive care companion app built around shift planning, wellness tracking, partner check-ins, and a gentle study timer in one calm mobile experience.
projects.impact: Shows product thinking, empathy in software design, frontend implementation, and the ability to turn a personal care idea into a complete Android-ready app.
projects.role: Product concept, frontend development, mobile UX, Android packaging, and partner-sharing flow design
highlights: Combined shift planning, wellness tracking, partner check-ins, and a gentle study timer in one mobile flow
Built a calm interface with reusable screens, dark mode support, and supportive copy
Prepared the app for Android delivery with Capacitor plus Supabase-backed sharing and reminders

details.problem: Long and draining shifts can make it hard to keep up with care routines, study focus, and partner communication in one manageable place.
details.solution: Build a soft, supportive care companion app that brings shift planning, wellness tracking, partner check-ins, and a gentle study timer together in one calm mobile experience.
details.architecture: React frontend -> local and product state -> Supabase Auth and Postgres for partner sharing -> Capacitor Android package -> local notifications and reminder flows.
details.software: React 19 and TypeScript interface built with Vite, packaged through Capacitor for Android, with Supabase handling auth, partner sync, and reminder-related features.
results: Created a working Android-ready care companion app
Covered core flows such as shift planning, wellness signals, partner sharing, and study support
Built experience with frontend architecture, state handling, notifications, and Android packaging
challenges: Kept the interface calm and simple instead of overloading it with too many features
Balanced emotional context with a practical app structure that still feels usable every day
Designed partner-aware sharing and reminder flows without losing the personal tone of the app

projects.name: KKB Snap
projects.summary: A cross-platform receipt-splitting app with receipt scanning, live item claiming, proportional bill calculation, and payment QR handoff.
projects.impact: Makes shared receipts easier to scan, divide, claim, calculate, and settle in real time.
projects.role: Product development, frontend implementation, OCR integration, and realtime backend integration
highlights: Scans receipts with Mindee OCR
Supports live item claiming and proportional bill calculation
Provides payment QR handoff and real-time shared expense data

details.problem: Manually entering receipt items, tracking claims, and calculating each person's share makes group payments slow and error-prone.
details.solution: Scan the receipt, let participants claim items live, calculate proportional totals, and hand off payment through a QR flow.
details.architecture: React Native and Expo interface -> Mindee OCR receipt extraction -> Supabase PostgreSQL and Realtime -> proportional calculation -> payment QR handoff.
details.software: TypeScript, React Native, Expo Router, Supabase Auth, PostgreSQL, Realtime, Edge Functions, and Mindee OCR.
results: Built an end-to-end host and guest flow from authentication and receipt scanning through item claiming and settlement
Added realtime exclusive item claims, proportional tax and tip allocation, and centavo-exact reconciliation
Implemented GCash and Maya receive-QR handoff with fallback account details
challenges: Turning OCR output into a clean, editable receipt workflow
Synchronizing live item claims while keeping proportional totals accurate

projects.name: SENTIA
projects.summary: A local, privacy-first desktop AI assistant powered by Google Gemma 3 via Ollama, featuring engineering domain intelligence, persistent memory, and OS automation.
projects.impact: Empowers engineers with 100% offline, zero-cloud-leakage technical intelligence, circuit calculation solvers, and native OS automation in a modern glassmorphic interface.
projects.role: Desktop application architecture, Electron & React frontend, Node IPC dispatch logic, Ollama LLM integration, and electronics engineering prompt engineering
highlights: Runs locally with zero cloud API reliance using Ollama and Google Gemma 3 (1B/4B)
Features dedicated Engineering Mode for RC filter calculations, ESP32 pinout matrices, and circuit math
Includes secure whitelisted OS system control and persistent multi-session memory storage

details.problem: Commercial AI assistants require constant internet access, introduce latency, and risk leaking proprietary engineering data, circuit schematics, and personal codebases to third-party clouds.
details.solution: Build a native desktop application combining Electron, React, and local Ollama inference with Google Gemma, equipped with domain-specific engineering tools and safe local OS system control.
details.architecture: React User Interface -> Electron Preload Bridge -> Main Process IPC Handlers -> Local Ollama REST API (localhost:11434) -> Google Gemma 3 inference engine; Child Process executor with strict command whitelist; Persistent JSON sessions in ~/.sentia/.
details.software: Electron runtime with contextIsolation and webSecurity enabled, React UI with custom dark glassmorphic styling, Node.js IPC channels, Ollama local REST client, regex-based intent classification, and formula solver modules.
results: Achieved responsive local inference (~42ms per token) on consumer hardware without internet connectivity
Integrated specialized engineering calculation helpers for cut-off frequencies, resonance, and Ohm's law
Protected user data with 100% on-device session storage and whitelisted action execution
challenges: Preventing unauthorized command execution by enforcing a strict command whitelist and argument isolation
Balancing Electron memory footprint while sustaining concurrent Ollama streaming responses
Designing an intuitive glassmorphic interface that accommodates both technical terminal output and natural conversational flow

projects.name: Log Pose TCG
projects.summary: A mobile-first collection tracker, card pricing intelligence app, and deck builder for One Piece Trading Card Game players and collectors.
projects.impact: Solves collector pricing uncertainty with automated Japanese market (Yuyutei) currency conversion, collection portfolio valuation, and multi-set card indexing.
projects.role: Mobile frontend architecture, Riverpod state management, Supabase integration, card data normalization, and market price pipeline
highlights: Built mobile-first collection management with live PHP portfolio valuation and analytics
Integrated real-time card database with set filters, rarity sorting, and multi-select addition
Synchronized Japanese Yuyutei market prices and Limitless TCG datasets through automated pipeline

details.problem: TCG collectors and competitive players in the Philippines struggle to find accurate, up-to-date Japanese card values, track high-value binder portfolios, and search across rapid set releases.
details.solution: Develop a dedicated Flutter mobile application featuring real-time market pricing in PHP/JPY, multi-set card filtering, quick-select collection adding, and tournament deck creation.
details.architecture: Flutter Mobile UI (Riverpod + GoRouter) -> Supabase PostgreSQL DB -> Automated Card Ingest Pipeline (Limitless TCG scraper + Yuyutei price matching) -> Real-time Portfolio Valuation Engine.
details.software: Flutter SDK 3.4+, Riverpod state management, Supabase Auth & PostgreSQL, GoRouter navigation, Caching image layers, and Node.js card sync workers with cron automation.
results: Indexed comprehensive One Piece TCG sets from OP-01 through current expansions
Delivered instant search with color, rarity, leader, and attribute filtering
Integrated collection analytics tracking total binder value, unique card count, and monthly value shifts
challenges: Matching disparate card naming conventions between English releases and Japanese Yuyutei catalog numbers
Maintaining smooth, 60fps scrolling performance across large card image grids on budget mobile devices
Designing an additive multi-select card addition workflow without disrupting the existing card browsing experience

projects.name: TapAndGo — NFC Review & Landing Platform
projects.summary: A smart NFC contactless business card and landing page system that turns physical taps into instant 5-star Google reviews and social follows for local cafes.
projects.impact: Supercharges in-person customer conversion for local businesses by bridging physical NFC tap hardware with high-converting mobile micro-sites and automated Google Places review scrapers.
projects.role: End-to-end founder & developer: physical NFC card programming, mobile-responsive landing pages, headless Puppeteer review scraper, and client admin CMS
highlights: Programmed NTAG215/216 NFC physical cards and dynamic QR backup routing directly to review workflows
Engineered ultra-fast, mobile-first brand landing micro-sites with instant Google Review intent launchers
Built automated Puppeteer scraper extracting live Google Maps business ratings, operating hours, and customer reviews

details.problem: Brick-and-mortar cafes and retail shops struggle to collect positive Google reviews at the point of sale because asking customers to search and rate manually causes over 90% drop-off.
details.solution: Deploy pre-programmed NFC tap cards and counter stands that instantly trigger a streamlined mobile landing page or direct Google Review rating prompt the second a phone is tapped.
details.architecture: Customer taps physical NFC Card -> Smartphone reads NDEF URL -> Micro-landing page renders cached business profile -> 1-click Google Review modal triggers native Maps/Browser rating dialog; Puppeteer scraper refreshes live reviews and operating hours periodically into client configuration.
hardware: NTAG215 and NTAG216 high-frequency (13.56MHz) NFC PVC Cards
Acrylic counter tap stands with embedded NFC antenna tags
details.software: Modern JavaScript with Tailwind CSS design tokens, Node.js & Express server, Puppeteer-core headless browser automation for Google Maps extraction, Supabase client configuration store, and a client self-service admin portal.
results: Successfully launched live production client deployments including Kape Session (Sta. Elena, Marikina City)
Streamlined review submission flow from a 4-step search process into a single tap
Created unified multi-client tenant system with client configuration JSON schemas
challenges: Bypassing aggressive Google Maps anti-bot challenge walls without paid Enterprise API overhead using specialized headless Chromium flags
Optimizing initial HTML/CSS load time under 300ms so customer smartphones open the review prompt instantaneously upon physical tap
Handling different NFC antenna positions and OS permission prompts between iOS Safari and Android Chrome

projects.name: Smart Pet Feeder System
projects.summary: An automated feeding prototype using ultrasonic and LDR sensing, servo-controlled dispensing, buzzer alerts, and OLED status feedback.
projects.impact: Demonstrates practical automation with sensing, actuation, feedback, and user-visible system state.
projects.role: Hardware logic, sensor-actuator integration, prototype feedback flow
highlights: Used ultrasonic and light sensing to support feeding decisions
Controlled servo motors for dispensing actions
Added buzzer and OLED feedback for user awareness

details.problem: Pet feeding can be inconsistent when owners are busy or away, especially without a simple way to see system status.
details.solution: Create a sensor-assisted feeder that controls dispensing, reports status, and alerts users during operation.
details.architecture: Sensors -> microcontroller decision logic -> servo dispensing -> buzzer and OLED feedback.
details.software: Control logic for sensor readings, dispensing timing, servo movement, notification states, and OLED status messages.
results: Built an automated dispensing flow with clear local feedback
Combined sensing and actuation in a complete physical prototype
challenges: Coordinated timing between sensor reads, servo movement, and feedback
Used display and buzzer states to make the device easier to understand during testing
